- **1.5.0-rc.1**: release candidate for 1.5.0. **No engine change** --
  `Signal.js` and `Signal.d.ts` are FROZEN: byte-identical to beta.8, hot paths
  byte-identical to 1.4.0. This RC brings the torture surface to full **parity
  with 1.4.4**: `bench/torture/run.mjs` now registers the complete **22-scenario
  suite (19 semantic + 3 soak)**, up from the sixteen (13 semantic + 3 soak) the
  earlier RC listed. Six scenarios are finalised here -- `owner-torture`
  (getOwner/runWithOwner capture-restore + ABA degradation), `error-torture`
  (throwing effect bodies: per-effect buffering, exact-order AggregateError,
  buffer drain over 4096 cycles), `deep-chain-torture` (pullComputed recursion
  fail-closed with a RangeError vs the iterative push path), `zerogc-torture`
  (the zero-GC hot path made falsifiable via `@zakkster/lite-gc-profiler` --
  a **dev-only** dependency), `introspect-torture` (describe/forEach*/ownerOf +
  the ABA gen-stamp guard), and `lifecycle-torture` (createRoot detachment +
  destroy registry reset). This is **verification-only**: the new files OBSERVE
  the frozen engine and pin its actual behaviour; nothing in the engine moved.
  A notable milestone -- several lanes that only ever SKIPPED on earlier cuts
  EXECUTE on the 1.5.0 engine for the FIRST TIME: `box-torture`
  (signalBox/computedBox), the `churn-box` lane inside `zerogc-torture`
  (signalBox create+dispose churn retains 0 B/call), and the owner/root
  lifecycle scenarios `lifecycle-torture` + `owner-torture` (via
  getOwner/runWithOwner/createRoot). On the 1.5.0 engine the runner executes
  **15 semantic** scenarios and reports a clean SKIP for the four feature-gated
  later-version ones (`scope-torture` 1.6.0, `flush-torture` 1.8.0,
  `cleanup-return-torture` 1.9.0, `dispose-torture` 1.10.0) -- verified green:
  **22/22 passed** (19 semantic + 3 soak, zero errors, pools back to their
  leaf-only floor; each soak now carries an Int32Array value-oracle sweep with
  zero mismatches). Unit suite is **461 tests: 460 pass + 1 skip** (SSR N/A in
  `17-reactivity`) with the sibling `@zakkster/lite-devtools` present, including
  the new 7-test `test/29-throwing-equals` that pins the three `equals()` call
  sites. Nothing new ships: `files[]` excludes `bench/` and `dependencies` stays
  empty (zero runtime deps), so the publishable surface is byte-identical to
  beta.8 apart from version strings. Drop-in over 1.5.0-beta.8.

- **1.5.0-beta.8**: the **torture-surface bump**. No engine change --
  the only edit to `Signal.js` is the version string in its banner. The torture
  suite (one runner `bench/torture/run.mjs`, `semantic` / `soak` groups, shared
  `helpers/`) gains a sixth semantic scenario, **`box-torture`**, for the
  `signalBox` / `computedBox` surface. It runs the same differential fuzz as
  `oracle-fuzzer` but realises every node in the random DAG as EITHER a callable
  or a box, checked against an independent uncached reference that does not know
  which is which -- the only test that exercises box<->callable divergence in a
  mixed graph. Mutation-verified: a `computedBox` whose default equality silently
  downgrades from `Object.is` to `===` is caught by `box-torture` alone (33/300
  seeds); the box unit suite (`24-signalbox`, now fully live, 12/12) and the
  callable-only `oracle-fuzzer` (400/400) both pass it. Unit total is now **453
  pass, 1 skip** (the SSR N/A in `17-reactivity`), up from 405 on 1.4.1. Nothing
  here ships: `files[]` excludes `bench/`. Drop-in over 1.5.0-beta.2.

- **1.5.0-beta.2**: the re-attach companion to `createRoot`.
  **`getOwner()`** and **`runWithOwner(ownerHandle, fn)`** land as registry
  methods + top-level bindings. **No engine change** from 1.5.0-beta.1 -- the
  hot-path function bodies (`pullComputed`, `markDownstream`, `executeEffect`,
  `flushEffects`, `allocateLink`, `severTail`, `createNode`, `runCleanup`,
  `disposeNode`) are byte-identical (sha256-verified over extracted bodies).
  The two new primitives are ~20 lines of user-API code + two top-level
  bindings; `currentOwner` is read/written at the same sites as before
  (creation adoption, effect-body save/restore, cleanup) plus the two new
  wrappers. Drop-in over 1.5.0-beta.1.

  **Handles are gen-stamped, not raw pointers.** `getOwner()` returns a
  `describeNode` handle stamped with the pool slot's `NODE_GEN`;
  `runWithOwner` resolves via `liveNode()` (the same ABA-guard machinery
  `describe` / `nodeId` / `forEachOwned` / `ownerOf` have used since 1.2.1).
  Stale, null, undefined, or non-tracker (signal) handles all degrade to
  **rooted execution**: `currentOwner` set to `null`, `fn` runs, created
  children survive without adoption, caller disposes them (same contract
  as `createRoot`). This matters because node objects are pooled and the
  LIFO free list recycles a disposed owner's slot into the next
  effect/computed allocated. A raw-pointer alternative
  (`getOwner() { return currentOwner; }`) fails two hazards, both pinned
  in `test/28-run-with-owner.test.mjs` and empirically reproduced by
  `harness/owner-hazard-repro.mjs`:
    (i) **Recycled-slot cascade death** -- owner A captured; A disposed;
        stranger B allocated (LIFO -> A's slot); `runWithOwner(captured)`
        silently adopts continuation into B; B's next re-run
        cascade-disposes it. Measured on the unsafe engine: continuation
        ran 1 time before stranger disposal, 1 time after (should be 2
        then 3).
    (ii) **Corpse adoption = engine crash** -- capture; A disposed; slot
         NOT yet recycled; `runWithOwner(captured, () => effect(...))`
         splices a child into a disposed owner's `firstOwned`; next
         disposal walk recurses without termination.
         `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` at `runCleanup` /
         `disposeNode`. Not a leak; a crash.
  Both hazards degrade to rooted execution on the shipped implementation.

  **Semantics.** `runWithOwner` nulls the tracking observer + tracking flag
  for the duration of `fn` (same pairing `createRoot` uses). Reads directly
  in `fn` do not link to any enclosing observer; if the caller wants
  tracking under the restored owner, they nest an inner effect/computed in
  `fn` which establishes its own scope. Returns whatever `fn` returns.
  Restores previous owner/observer/tracking triplet on return AND on
  throw. Signal handles are rejected (`runWithOwner(signalHandle, fn)` ->
  rooted execution) because signals cannot own -- the `flags & (FLAG_COMPUTED
  | FLAG_EFFECT)` check gates adoption. `getOwner()` returns `undefined`
  (not `null`) outside any effect/computed body to match the shape of the
  other handle-taking APIs. **Tests:** 455 total (439 pre-existing + 16
  new), 444 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip (SSR N/A), 10 cancelled (`25-devtools-
  real-boot` cases needing the devtools peer dep -- pre-existing).
  **Watch.js needs no changes**: `watch` / `when` / `whenAsync` create
  effects through the normal path and inherit correct adoption under
  `runWithOwner` automatically.

- **1.5.0-beta.1** (was "current" before beta.2): the **API-surface minor**. Two non-callable,
  allocation-light primitives -- `signalBox(initial, opts?)` returning
  `{ get, set, peek, update, subscribe }` and `computedBox(fn, opts?)` returning
  `{ get, peek, subscribe }` -- land alongside the callable `signal` / `computed`,
  plus **`createRoot(fn)`** as the ownership escape hatch. **The callable API and
  hot paths are unchanged from 1.4.0**; `stats()` grows to **13 keys** -- adds
  `nodePoolPopulation` / `linkPoolPopulation` (the true constructed-object counts,
  distinct from the `*Capacity` ledgers). This is an
  additive surface, not a second engine. Boxes wrap the same `ReactiveNode` and
  interoperate freely with callables in one graph (verified both directions);
  ownership, batching, glitch-freedom, and introspection apply uniformly, and box
  nodes count in `stats().signals` / `computeds` exactly as callable nodes. Box
  construction is ~1.7x cheaper than the callable (an `Object.create(proto)` handle
  with two own props added in fixed order -- never `setPrototypeOf`, which would
  transition the object to dictionary mode and blow the method-call ICs to
  megamorphic); the read/write hot path stays zero-GC (200k box writes through a
  256-wide graph: 0 heap growth, 0 pool growths). `createRoot` runs `fn` with
  `currentOwner` and `currentObserver` (and the tracking flag) nulled, so
  effects/computeds created directly in `fn` are not adopted by the enclosing owner
  and survive its re-runs/disposal -- the sanctioned opt-out for lazily spawning a
  long-lived watcher from inside a consumer effect (`lite-query`'s pattern);
  unwrapped, the consumer owns the watcher and cascade-disposes it. Inner
  effect/computed bodies still establish their own scopes; `createRoot` returns
  whatever `fn` returns. The owner/observer split (1.2.0) made `currentOwner` and
  `currentObserver` distinct precisely so ownership could be detached without
  affecting tracking; `createRoot` is the first of the two named primitives
  (`runWithOwner`, the re-attach half, is not yet shipped). The `24-signalbox`
  suite (staged `{skip:true}` since 1.3.0) now runs and passes. **Tests:** 439
  total, 438 pass, 0 fail, **1 skip** (only the architecturally-N/A SSR case in
  `17-reactivity`; the 9 originally-staged signalBox tests are now active and
  the suite carries box-coverage additions plus the 1.5.0 coverage-closure block
  in `test/12-coverage.test.mjs`, and `createRoot` tests in
  `test/27-create-root.test.mjs`). **Coverage:** `Signal.js`
  100% statements / 100% branches / 100% functions / 100% lines; `Watch.js` 100%
  (rc coverage pass; reconfirm under codify). Drop-in over 1.4.0.
  **VersionMatrix (identical-code guard, new in 1.5.0-beta):** the
  `harness/VersionMatrix/` regression gate now records the sha256 of the engine
  source at every capture (`baselines/<label>/engine.sha256`). If the candidate's
  hash matches a baseline's, that axis runs the *same bytes* and the gate marks
  it `SKIP` rather than let variance flag a phantom regression. Genuine code
  changes produce a different hash and are gated normally. Everything else about
  the harness -- cold-process-per-version, LCG-deterministic input, two baselines
  (floor `1.3.0` + rolling `1.5.0-alpha.1`), calibrated tolerances (`frame.avg`
  5% rolling / 10% floor, `frame.p99` and `phase.write.p99` 18% / 30%), four
  workloads mapping to public bench claims -- carries forward from 1.4.0. Run by
  hand (`npm run gate`); not wired into a publish hook.
  **Bench harness (protocol v3):** rebuilt around three fixed-config instruments -- microscope (`benchmark.mjs`, recommended eager config, six first-party shapes), mirror (`mirror.mjs` + `sweep.mjs`, Andrii's canonical adapter verbatim, rows diff 1:1 against his log), version-economics (`harness/toe-to-toe`) -- each output carrying a machine-generated `#STAMP` (engine + harness sha256, live registry config, host, node). Pre-v3 five-framework suite retained one release as `bench-reactive-legacy` (deprecated; removed after 1.5.1). Methodology in `bench/README.md`.
  **Bench position (1.5.0-beta history, Andrii's host; superseded by the current position in "Benchmark snapshot" below)** (third-party
  [js-reactivity-benchmark](https://github.com/volynetstyle/js-reactivity-benchmark),
  15 frameworks, 47 tests; fresh 1.5.0-beta run, raw log
  `bench/AndriiVolynetsReactiveBench.log`): #4 by geomean (79.3) at 1.75x behind
  alien-signals (1.00x, 45.2), reflex (1.08x, 48.9), @reactively (1.33x, 59.9);
  ahead of 5th-place Preact Signals (99.8, lite ~21% ahead -- the gap widened
  after Preact's own regression on the newer 1.14.2 in this sweep). Ahead of @vue/reactivity (1.5x),
  Signia (1.7x), MobX (2.2x), @solidjs/signals (3.2x), SolidJS (4.6x). Top-3 on
  25/47 tests (up from 23 on 1.4.0). Outright winners this sweep (rank 1 of all
  15) on TWO shapes: `createComputations4to1` (a computed-creation micro; lite
  edges alien 7.08ms vs 7.10ms) and `1000x5 - 25 sources (wide dense)` (the
  "large web app / wide dense" pattern from the propagation bench). Rank 2 on
  another nine shapes (broadPropagation, diamond, repeatedObservers, unstable
  propagation, `manySourcesIntoOneComputedEffect`, `manySourcesIntoOneDirectEffect`,
  `molBench`, `32x8 - 4 sources - pull`, and `10x5 - 2 sources - read 20%` simple
  component). The outright-win count fluctuates
  at the top of a very tight leaderboard where alien-signals, reflex, and lite
  trade sub-percent margins per shape (1.4.0 sweep had lite outright on 5
  shapes; this sweep 2); the geomean rank at #4 has held across every published
  sweep and is the honest stable metric. (The suite measures reactivity
  libraries -- Vue reactivity core, MobX, Solid, Preact Signals -- not full UI
  frameworks like React/Angular.)
  In the community reactive suite (median-of-10, raw runs in
  `bench/bench-runs-reactive/run_1.txt` ... `run_10.txt`), fastest of 5
  frameworks on the entire `dyn:*` family (the realistic large-DOM-framework
  shapes): dyn: simple 433.17ms (+19% vs alien), dynamic 311.74ms (+16%), large
  web app 539.05ms (+9%), wide dense 874.01ms (+6%), deep 333.06ms (+12%).
  **Lite now leads alien on ALL 7 `S: updateComputations` rows this sweep**
  (+3%/+6%/+3%/+12%/+3%/+2%/+8%; was 4/7 on 1.4.0). Behind on the
  construction-cost path (`S: createComputations*`, `cellx`, `createDataSignals`).
  Third-party engine versions bumped since the 1.4.0 sweep (alien-signals
  3.1.2 -> 3.2.1, @preact/signals-core 1.14.1 -> 1.14.2, @vue/reactivity
  3.5.13 -> 3.5.35, solid-js 1.9.12 -> 1.9.13); any within-lib delta reflects
  those bumps + host noise, not lite-signal changes (1.4.0 -> 1.5.0 hot paths
  are byte-identical).

- **1.4.0** (drop-in over 1.3.0): the **observability minor**. `stats()` gains three
  cumulative lifecycle counters -- `totalAllocations`, `totalDisposals`,
  `poolGrowths` -- the surface reserved for 1.4.0 in the 1.2.x/1.3.0 notes, now
  delivered. **The hot paths and public callable API are byte-identical to 1.3.0**;
  the counters bump on existing acquire / dispose / pool-grow edges that already
  ran, never on the steady-state read path, so throughput and zero-GC are
  unchanged. The 1.3.0 eager pool default carries forward (`prealloc: "eager"`).
  **`stats()` now returns 11 keys** (the 8 live gauges plus the 3 counters).
  `totalAllocations` counts every node acquired (pool pop OR fresh build);
  `totalDisposals` counts every node returned to the pool, with
  `totalAllocations - totalDisposals === activeNodes` in a quiescent registry;
  `poolGrowths` counts pool-growth chunks (node OR link crossing its ledger) --
  nonzero after warm-up means the initial pool was undersized, 0 means an eager pool
  was sized right. All three are monotonic and zeroed only by `destroy()` (1.6.0: `reset()` keeps them; totalDisposals grows). They are
  exact, not sampled: a consumer sampling `stats()` over time derives allocation
  rate (delta totalAllocations / delta t), pool-reuse ratio
  (1 - poolGrowths*initialCap/totalAllocations), and churn without the engine
  computing rates -- the series lite-devtools 1.2 / lite-studio 1.2 plot. **Tests:**
  429 total, 419 pass, 0 fail, 10 skip (6 new counter tests in `test/03-pool.test.mjs`
  cover the 13-key shape (1.5.0: +nodePoolPopulation/+linkPoolPopulation), the live invariant, poolGrowths firing on growth vs staying
  0 on a sized eager pool, and destroy() reset). **Coverage:** `Signal.js` 100%
  statements / 98.26% branches / 100% functions / 100% lines; `Watch.js` 100%.
  Drop-in over 1.3.0.

- **1.3.0** (drop-in over 1.2.2): the **pool minor**. Node and link pools become
  growable and incrementally populated; the propagation mark phase moves to an
  intrusive linked-list stack (a `nextMark` field); a small registry config surface
  (`prealloc`, `onCapacityExceeded`, `maxFlushPasses`) is exposed. The hot paths and
  public callable API are byte-identical to 1.2.2 -- everything here is
  pool mechanics, construction-time behavior, and new opt-in config. Steady-state
  zero-GC is unchanged: after warm-up the pools recycle exactly as before.
  **`prealloc` (`"eager"` default | `"lazy"`):** `"eager"` constructs the full
  `maxNodes` / `maxLinks` pools up front -- deterministic latency, zero allocation
  inside any subsequent hot path (the 16ms / 120fps render-frame contract), at the
  cost of a larger resident heap every major GC traces. `"lazy"` treats the
  capacities as ledgers, constructs nodes/links on first demand, recycles through
  the free lists thereafter -- smaller heap, faster cold start, lighter GC marking,
  identical zero-GC steady state after warm-up. **Growable pools
  (`onCapacityExceeded: "grow"`):** pools extend past their initial capacity via
  chunked refill -- contiguous runs of up to 1024 links / 256 nodes per free-list
  miss, not a single doubling burst, so any one growth pause stays bounded
  (~chunk x ~0.5us). The growth path no longer length-extends the effect queues
  or mark stack (which permanently converted them PACKED->HOLEY). Link growth is
  bounded by the hard `maxLinks * 16` ceiling; `"throw"` (default, now backed by a
  named `CapacityError`) preserves the 1.2.x fail-fast behavior.
  **`maxFlushPasses`** (default 100) is now a public config -- the cycle-protection
  ceiling that throws an `Error` prefixed `"CycleError:"`. **Intrusive mark stack:**
  `markDownstream` walks an iterative DFS backed by a `nextMark` field on each node
  instead of an external `markStack` array; behaviorally identical (same nodes, same
  order, same glitch-free guarantee), and the write lands in the cache line already
  hot from reading `markEpoch`. `nextMark` is the only node-shape change in 1.3.0.
  **`stats()` shape unchanged** (8 keys: `signals`, `computeds`, `effects`,
  `activeNodes`, `activeLinks`, `pooledLinks`, `nodePoolCapacity`,
  `linkPoolCapacity`); the capacity keys are ledgers under `"lazy"`. Cumulative
  allocation counters (`totalAllocations` / `totalDisposals` / `poolGrowths`) remain
  reserved for 1.4.0 and are still absent. **Tests:** 423 total, 413 pass, 0 fail,
  10 skip (the 10 skips are 9 signalBox-staged-for-1.5.0 in
  `test/24-signalbox.test.mjs` plus 1 architecturally-N/A SSR case in
  `17-reactivity`); 4 new pool tests in `test/03-pool.test.mjs` cover the lazy
  on-demand / never-allocated-destroy / grow-extends-ledger / link-ceiling paths.
  **Coverage** (c8@11, Node 22): `Signal.js` 100% statements / 98.26% branches /
  100% functions / 100% lines; `Watch.js` 100% across all four. Behavior-
  preservation difftest: 20,000 direct + 10,000 batched writes vs the published
  1.1.5 reference, 0 disagreements -- pool growth, chunked refill, and the intrusive
  mark stack do not alter observable propagation. Drop-in over 1.2.2.

- **1.2.2**: `createNode` clean-free-list invariant audit. Removes
  ten redundant field-writes that defended against a state the engine cannot
  produce on a clean free-list: seven graph/batch fields (`headDep`, `tailDep`,
  `headSub`, `tailSub`, `revertEpoch`, `preBatchValue`, `preBatchVersion`) and
  three owner-tree fields (the non-adoption `firstOwned`, the adoption-path
  `prevOwned`, and the else-branch `owner`). Both teardown paths
  (`disposeNode` direct, `runCleanup` cascade) already null these fields, and
  the `ReactiveNode` constructor initializes them to the same values on the
  fresh-pool-growth path -- so the redundant writes in `createNode` were
  defense against a state that cannot exist. **No public surface change, no
  semantic change.** New `test/26-free-list-invariant.test.mjs` (3 invariant
  tests + 1 targeted coverage test for the swallow-on-self-dispose-then-throw
  branch in `pullComputed`) asserts the invariant directly by inspecting
  freshly-allocated nodes via the documented `describe()` -> `NODE_PTR`
  introspection protocol; new `test/25-devtools-real-boot.test.mjs` (10 tests)
  boots the actual `Devtools.js` against the 1.2.2 engine and pins the 1.2.x
  introspection contract for downstream tooling, including the 8-key
  `stats()` shape (`signals`, `computeds`, `effects`, `activeNodes`,
  `activeLinks`, `pooledLinks`, `nodePoolCapacity`, `linkPoolCapacity`).
  408 tests total: 398 pass, 10 skip, 0 fail (the 10 skips are 9
  signalBox-staged-for-1.5.0 in `test/24-signalbox.test.mjs` plus 1
  architecturally-N/A SSR case in `17-reactivity`). Coverage on `Signal.js`:
  100% statements / 98.43% branches / 100% functions / 100% lines; `Watch.js`
  100% across all four (c8@11, Node 22) -- a branch-coverage gain over the
  1.2.1 baseline (98.07%), from the targeted swallow-on-self-dispose-then-throw
  test in `pullComputed`.
  Version lineage:
  this is the engine previously labeled `1.2.3` in dev -- renumbered to
  `1.2.2` because the deletion is small, isolated, and intentionally
  non-behavioral. Drop-in over 1.2.1. **Bench position (1.2.2-era history, Andrii's host; superseded by the current position in "Benchmark snapshot" below)** (third-party
  [js-reactivity-benchmark](https://github.com/volynetstyle/js-reactivity-benchmark),
  15 frameworks, 47 tests): #4 by geomean (75.5) at 1.77x behind alien-signals
  (1.00x), reflex (1.15x), @reactively (1.39x); now ahead of 5th-place Preact
  Signals (79.2, lite ~5% ahead -- the gap widened from 1.2.x). Ahead of @vue/reactivity (1.5x),
  Signia (1.7x), MobX (2.3x), @solidjs/signals (2.7x), SolidJS (4.2x). Top-3 on
  21/47 tests; outright winner on `manyEffectsFromOneSource`,
  `manySourcesIntoOneComputedEffect`, and
  `manySourcesIntoOneComputedEffectWithDirect` (and edges the leader alien on a
  fourth, the 1-source linear-chain pull). (The suite measures reactivity
  libraries -- Vue reactivity core, MobX, Solid, Preact Signals -- not full UI
  frameworks like React/Angular.)
  In the community reactive suite (median-of-10), fastest of 5 frameworks
  on the entire `dyn:*` family (the realistic large-DOM-framework shapes)
  and the entire `S: updateComputations*` family. Behind on the
  construction-cost path (`S: createComputations*`, `cellx`, `createDataSignals`).

- **1.2.1**: correctness-and-introspection patch. Drop-in over 1.2.0;
  no public surface removed. **Stale-handle introspection (ABA fix):** the v1.2.0
  owner tree made the engine recycle pool slots autonomously on owner re-run, so
  holding a stale handle stopped being a user error and became a routine
  occurrence. Pre-1.2.1, `nodeId`/`describe`/`forEachObserver`/`forEachSource`/
  `hasObservers`/`observeObservers`/`peek()` would resolve `NODE_PTR` ungated
  and happily report the recycled slot's NEW resident through an old handle
  (wrong id, wrong value, wrong edges). All six entry points + `peek()` + `read()`
  + `set()` now resolve through a generation check (the same ABA discipline
  `dispose()` already had); stale handles read as `undefined` (or throw the
  documented `TypeError`, for `observeObservers`). Since 1.6.0 a tracked read that disposes its own node from hook code (onConnect / onGraphMutation / tail-sever onDisconnect, run by the new dependency link) also returns `undefined` (LEDGER #44). `describe()` descriptors are
  gen-stamped alongside `NODE_PTR`, so the "descriptors are re-walkable handles"
  contract survives the guard: a fresh descriptor walks, one held across a
  recycle correctly goes stale. **Added -- `onGraphMutation(fn)`:** registry-level
  (and top-level) graph-mutation hook for push-based tooling. Single nullable
  listener (since 1.6.0: a live-entry stack, newest live listener active, unsubscribe in any order); every fire point is `if (mutationHook !== null) mutationHook(opcode, intA, intB)`
  -- zero-cost gate when absent, allocation-free dispatch when present. Opcodes:
  `1` node-create `(id, flags)`, `2` node-dispose `(id, flags)` (cascades
  included; since 1.6.0 `flags` can carry bit 6, `1 << 6`, the internal stale-read mark, when a node that a write flagged while it was mid-run is disposed before the flag clears (still mid-run, or after that run threw; its next run clears it); op 1 never does; box nodes also carry bit 7, `1 << 7` = 128, FLAG_BOX: 160 signalBox / 129 computedBox), `3` link-add `(source.id, target.id)` (since 1.6.0 emitted only for an edge that still exists when it fires, and also when an `onConnect` hook throws and leaves the edge live: after the hook, before its error propagates, not when the hook disposed an endpoint; op 2 implies the node's subscriber edges are gone, and no per-edge op 4 is emitted for them: bench/soak/mirror.mjs rule I3), `4` link-remove `(source.id, target.id)` (since 1.6.0 fired after the edge is unlinked and its link is pooled: inside the listener the edge is gone, `hasObservers` is false for the last edge and `activeLinks` is already decremented; a listener that throws leaves no half-freed link, the source's 1->0 `onDisconnect` is still delivered before the error surfaces, and a throwing `onDisconnect` replaces the listener's error; in a dispose walk (a handle's `stop()` or `dispose(handle)`) the throw aborts the walk: edges not yet reached stay linked (their sources stay observed) and the node stays counted in `stats().effects`; the handle's own `stop()` is latched after the throw and does nothing more, so finish the teardown with `dispose(handle)` (test/113 T2).),
  `5` recompute `(id, 0)` before each effect re-run / computed re-eval.
  Contract: observe only -- never throw, never mutate the graph from inside.
  This is the connection point lite-devtools 1.1 / lite-studio 1.1 use to go
  push-based. **Added -- `forEachOwned(handle, fn)` / `ownerOf(handle)`:** owner-
  tree introspection. `forEachOwned` iterates a node's owned children as
  re-walkable descriptors; `ownerOf` returns the owner's descriptor or
  `undefined` (top-level or stale). Same descriptor conventions as
  `forEachObserver`/`forEachSource`; garbage input is a no-op/`undefined`.
  Also: `Object.is` hoisted to a module-level const (one IC entry instead of
  per-call lookup in `signal()`/`computed()`). 404 tests, **100% line / 98.07%
  branch coverage** on `Signal.js` + `Watch.js`. New
  `test/21-perf-pins.test.mjs` (6 tests -- construction-shape + ABA-guard pins),
  `test/22-mutation-hook.test.mjs` (12 tests -- `onGraphMutation` registration,
  the 5 opcodes, payload shape, registry isolation), and
  `test/23-owner-introspection.test.mjs` (14 tests -- `forEachOwned`, `ownerOf`,
  and gen-guarded behaviour across the introspection surface). Differential
  fuzz vs the published 1.1.5: 0 disagreements over 30,000 writes.

- **1.2.0**: structural refactor (three named layers: graph topology /
  ownership / propagation) plus four additive features built on top. Drop-in over
  1.1.5; no public surface removed. **Owner tree:** an effect or computed that
  creates nested observers (effect/computed) now owns them -- when the owner
  re-runs or is disposed, the engine cascade-disposes those observers before
  the new run. Plain signals are deliberately NOT owner-adopted so lazy-
  allocation wrappers (lite-store keys, lite-form fields) continue to survive
  re-runs of the computed that allocated them. **Pre-batch revert (FIX-R, F5):** inside `batch(...)`, setting a signal back to its pre-batch value (under its `equals`) restores the old version and fires nothing ONLY IF none of the signal's current subscribers is running at the set back and none was re-evaluated since the signal's first write in the batch (`revertBlocked`, checked at the set back over the direct subscribers: `FLAG_COMPUTING`, or `evalVersion` past the `globalVersion` captured at that first write, plus the stamp cases below); otherwise the set back is a normal write (downstream re-runs and sees the reverted value). A body that ran in the batch but does not read the signal does not block its revert. A body that writes `s` and then reads `s` in the same run blocks the revert: through `FLAG_COMPUTING` while it runs, through its `evalVersion` (stamped past the capture) once it has returned (test/37 (c), the second case: `[5,0]`). The earlier KNOWN residuals (a) (running-body read) and (b) (30-bit body-run counter, k*2^30 runs) are closed (LEDGER #47, AUD-E2): the counter no longer exists. The check measures each subscriber's `evalVersion` from the capture as an int32-wrapped distance x = (evalVersion - capture) | 0 and blocks the revert when the subscriber is mid-run, x > 0 (re-evaluated after the capture), x <= -2^29 (a stamp 2^29 or more versions behind: a stale re-run's far-floor needs-run marker or a dormant stamp, which cannot be ordered against the capture), or `evalVersion` is 0 (an effect re-queued by a stale read). Only a stamp at the capture or fewer than 2^29 versions behind it lets the revert proceed (1.6.0, ARG-E2 F4; before it a stamp left across the 2^31 dormancy band let a revert through). It errs on the safe side: a stamp 2^29 or more behind blocks even when its reader saw nothing new (at most one extra run; test/114 R rows). KNOWN residual: a re-evaluation more than 2^32 - 2^29 version bumps after the capture, inside one batch, aliases into the revert window and is missed (derived from the compare, not gated). **AggregateError on
  multi-throw:** two or more effects throwing in the same flush pass aggregate to
  `AggregateError` at the trigger; single-throw is unchanged. **Scheduler thunk
  caching:** the scheduler closure is cached on the node and gen-bound, so async
  schedules that fire post-dispose against a recycled slot are guaranteed no-ops
  (ABA safe). Internal split: `currentObserver` and `currentOwner` are now
  distinct pointers (today they move together, no behavioural change). **Perf:**
  shared `peek` (one closure per registry instead of per primitive) shaves
  10-14% off signal/computed creation on the `S:create*` micros, no hot-path or
  behavioural change. 363 tests, 100% line / 98.62% branch coverage on
  `Signal.js` + `Watch.js`. Differential fuzz vs the published 1.1.5: 0
  disagreements over 30,000 writes. New `test/19-v12-additions.test.mjs`
  (24 tests) and `test/20-axis-stress.test.mjs` (23 tests -- eight orthogonal
  engine-invariant axes plus permanent conformance pins). **Conformance fixes
  in 1.2.0**: #141 (dispose during execution then continue: no re-run), and
  #238 / #241 / #243 (cleanup ordering on cascade: inner-before-outer,
  deepest-first, and the inner-only-re-run regression). #141 was a latent
  crash present in 1.1.5 too; the v1.2 owner tree exercised it more
  aggressively. Fix is two-fold -- nullify the tracking cursor in `disposeNode`
  when the disposed node is the active observer (plus a `gen`-snapshot guard
  in `executeEffect`/`pullComputed`); and swap `runCleanup` to cascade
  children first, then own.

- **1.1.5**: additive release in service of `@zakkster/lite-devtools` -- stable
  node identity on the introspection surface. `nodeId(handle)` -> the node's stable
  per-allocation id (the dedupe key for graph walks); `describe(handle)` -> the handle's
  own `{ id, kind, value }` descriptor, **re-walkable** (pass it back into
  `forEachObserver`/`forEachSource` to walk the full DAG); `forEach*` descriptors now carry
  `id`. One SMI write at allocation, node shape kept monomorphic -- **zero steady-state
  cost**. Drop-in over 1.1.4, no breaking changes. New `test/18-identity.test.mjs` (5 tests); plus `14-lifecycle-teardown`, `16-alien-parity`, and the `17-reactivity` behavioral suite.

- **1.1.4**: combined release -- a retracking rewrite plus an observer-lifecycle
  introspection surface. Drop-in over 1.1.3. **Retracking:** version-stamped O(1)
  reconciliation + a `markEpoch` clean-read short-circuit replace the cursor strategy's
  O(N)-per-dep degradation under chaotic high-fan-in batched read-after-write; stable read
  order is unchanged (still O(1), still zero-alloc). The two documented v1.1.x losses flipped
  to wins and are now fastest of five frameworks -- `dyn: large web app` 6194ms->571ms, `dyn:
  wide dense` 5115ms->912ms (verified by `retracking.difftest.mjs`: 20k direct + 10k batched, 0
  disagreements; no regressions elsewhere). **Introspection:** `hasObservers`,
  `observeObservers`, `forEachObserver`, `forEachSource` (top-level + per-registry), gated by
  an internal counter so zero steady-state cost when unused. New `test/13-introspection.test.mjs`
  (10 tests). Internally staged as 1.1.4 + 1.1.5; ships as a single 1.1.4.

- **1.1.3**: adds `isTracking()` (top-level + per-registry). Returns true iff a
  read right now would record a dependency (`isTrackingDeps && currentObserver !== null`).
  False inside `untrack`, `subscribe` callbacks, `onCleanup` bodies, `watch` /
  `when` callbacks, and outside any observer. ~1-2 ns. For wrapper libraries
  (lite-store, lite-query, lite-form) that allocate reactive primitives lazily
  on property reads. Per-registry: wrappers operating against a non-default
  registry must call THAT registry's `isTracking()`, not the top-level one.
  No behavior or engine changes.


- **1.1.2**: hot-path micro-optimizations, no behavior/API change.
  Inlined cursor fast-path in `signal`/`computed` reads (stable-order reads skip
  the `allocateLink` call); zero-allocation creation path (`opts` read defensively
  instead of defaulting to `{}`); single-closure `subscribe`. Owner-tree
  conformance items #209/#210 are wired but skipped pending the v1.2 ownership
  hybrid.

## When to use

- Animation loops, game HUDs, scoreboards, telemetry overlays.
- Twitch Extensions (1 MB bundle / 3 s cold start budget).
- Long-running browser sessions (millions of writes per session).
- Multi-tenant SDKs where each tenant needs an isolated reactive world.
- Any context where a GC pause breaks the frame budget.

## When NOT to use

- Server-side rendering -- no SSR story.
- Graph *construction* is allocation-heavy (per-node closures): on create-many micro-benchmarks `alien-signals` builds faster. Real apps build once and update forever -- lite-signal leads every dynamic-topology (`dyn:*`) row and trades the lead with alien within a few percent on the sub-60ms `S: updateComputations` micro-rows (noise-dominated). (The former "chaotic read order" caveat was closed in 1.1.4.)
- If you want time-travel or serialization -- build those on top. (Graph-inspection devtools are now buildable on the 1.1.4 introspection surface; see lite-devtools.)

## API summary

```ts
// Default registry helpers
function signal<T>(initial: T, opts?: { equals?: (a: T, b: T) => boolean }): Signal<T>;
function computed<T>(fn: () => T, opts?: { equals?: (a: T, b: T) => boolean }): Computed<T>;
function effect(fn: () => void, opts?: { scheduler?: (run: () => void) => void }): Dispose;
function signalBox<T>(initial: T, opts?: { equals?: (a: T, b: T) => boolean }): SignalBox<T>;   // 1.5.0
function computedBox<T>(fn: () => T, opts?: { equals?: (a: T, b: T) => boolean }): ComputedBox<T>; // 1.5.0
function createRoot<T>(fn: () => T): T;   // 1.5.0 -- detached ownership scope; returns fn's value
function createScope<T>(fn: (dispose: () => void) => T): T;   // 1.6.0 -- detached ADOPTING scope; one disposer for everything fn created
type Owner = NodeDescriptor | undefined;  // 1.5.0-beta.2 -- opaque, gen-stamped handle; safe across async gaps
function getOwner(): Owner;               // 1.5.0-beta.2 -- undefined outside any effect/computed body
function runWithOwner<T>(ownerHandle: Owner, fn: () => T): T;   // 1.5.0-beta.2 -- stale/null/signal-handle -> rooted execution
function dispose(api: Signal<any> | Computed<any> | SignalBox<any> | ComputedBox<any> | Dispose): void;
function batch<T>(fn: () => T): T;
function untrack<T>(fn: () => T): T;
function isTracking(): boolean;
function hasObservers(handle: Signal<any> | Computed<any>): boolean;
function observeObservers(
  handle: Signal<any> | Computed<any>,
  hooks?: { onConnect?: () => void; onDisconnect?: () => void }
): () => void;                          // returns idempotent unobserve; each call is an independent registration (1.6.0)
function forEachObserver(handle: Signal<any> | Computed<any>, fn: (d: NodeDescriptor) => void): void;
function forEachSource(handle: Signal<any> | Computed<any>, fn: (d: NodeDescriptor) => void): void;
function forEachOwned(handle: Signal<any> | Computed<any>, fn: (d: NodeDescriptor) => void): void;   // 1.2.1
function ownerOf(handle: Signal<any> | Computed<any>): NodeDescriptor | undefined;                    // 1.2.1
function nodeId(handle: Signal<any> | Computed<any>): number | undefined;            // 1.1.5
function describe(handle: Signal<any> | Computed<any>): NodeDescriptor | undefined;   // 1.1.5
function onGraphMutation(                                                              // 1.2.1
  fn: ((opcode: 1|2|3|4|5, intA: number, intB: number) => void) | null
): () => void;                                                                          // unsub any order; newest live listener active (since 1.6.0)
function onCleanup(fn: () => void): void;
function stats(): RegistryStats;
function destroy(): void;                        // 1.6.0: true shutdown; throws "graph not settled" in flight
function reset(): void;                          // 1.6.0: dispose every live node, keep the registry

// Registry construction
function createRegistry(config?: RegistryConfig): Registry;
function setDefaultRegistry(r: Registry): void;

// Snapshot / restore (1.6.0; top-level + per-registry). Plain in-process object, values by reference.
function snapshot(): Snapshot;                   // { v: 1, gv, nextId, nodes: [{ id, kind, flags, value, version, evalVersion, markEpoch, clean, ownerId, ownerPos, deps, subPos }] }
function restore(snap: Snapshot, opts?: { fnsById?: { [id: number]: Function }, handles?: { [id: number]: unknown }, config?: RegistryConfig }): Registry;
// snapshot() throws "graph not settled" in a flush, in a batch, in ANY running body (incl. under untrack / createRoot / runWithOwner; OPEN exception: a body that disposed its own node, LEDGER #53),
// inside onCleanup during a dispose / owner cascade or a reset() cleanup (destroy() runs no cleanups), inside an onGraphMutation listener, and while any effect has a pending scheduled run (queued or first run not yet executed).
// Reason suffixes: (flush/batch/track in progress) | (dispose in progress) | (onGraphMutation listener running) | (scheduled effect run pending).
// restore() builds a FRESH registry: no body runs, ids kept, effects NOT re-fired; a dirty computed restores with its recorded deps, value, version, error bit, evalVersion and markEpoch, so a read pulls it exactly as live does: the pull walks its deps and runs the body only if a dep moved past its evalVersion (otherwise the seeded value is a cache hit); when the body runs, a result equal to the seeded value (under Object.is -- a custom `equals` is not captured, so a computed built with one may propagate after restore where the live graph would not) does not propagate. A never-evaluated computed (version 0) is not seeded; its body runs on its first read. Restore places every subscriber link at its recorded position and each owner's children in recorded order, so each source's subscriber order and each owner's child order round-trip. After restore, the rebuilt graph runs each effect with the same sequence of values, and leaves every node with the same value or error and the same subscriber / owner order, as the live graph would from the same point; this is a gated property (the seeded live fuzz in test/76: 400 graphs x 3 seeds in `npm test`, 4000 x 5 seeds at the A9 close), not a universal law. Limits: cleanup callbacks (`onCleanup`) and a custom `equals` / scheduler are NOT captured, so an effect that registered a cleanup before `snapshot()` has none until its next run (the ORDER of pre-snapshot cleanups is therefore not reproduced); restore copies live state, so it reproduces live as it is now: LEDGER #38 (F6), #41 and #42 are fixed in 1.6.0-dev (FIX-T), so a restored graph's dependency pre-walk no longer rethrows a cached error either, leaving an error state is a change in it too, and a restored dep cycle throws CycleError (below).
// Missing fnsById entry / bad snapshot / duplicate id / dangling dep (any record, incl. dirty computeds) or owner id -> throws. Without config: maxNodes = max(1.5N+16, 1024),
// maxLinks = max(1.5L+16, 4 x maxNodes); source onCapacityExceeded / maxFlushPasses NOT carried.
// NOT captured: custom equals, effect schedulers (a restored effect runs synchronously unless re-created with one), onCleanup registrations, lifecycle / onGraphMutation listeners.
// fnsById bodies run in the RESTORED registry: call ITS untrack / batch / createRoot / runWithOwner (hold it in a `let r2` set from restore(); no body runs before restore returns). untrack is per-registry: another registry's untrack does not stop tracking in r2 (nor in live), so the read is tracked.
// restore() validates the whole snapshot before building anything: ids must be positive integers <= 0x3FFFFFFF (2^30 - 1) and unique; dep ids and ownerIds must be positive integers <= 0x3FFFFFFF that resolve to a record id; versions and flags must be int32; the snapshot's `gv`, `nextId` and every record's `evalVersion` / `markEpoch` are required and must be int32 (a missing or non-int32 one throws a TypeError before anything is built); `gv` is never 0, `nextId` may be any 32-bit integer, even at or below a restored id (live's counter wraps), and restore continues ids from it exactly, an effect's `evalVersion` is never 0, a signal's `evalVersion` and `markEpoch` are 0, `clean` must equal (`evalVersion !== 0` and `markEpoch` not modularly ahead of `evalVersion`), and a computed has `evalVersion` 0 exactly when its `version` is 0 (negative stamps after an int32 wrap and any stamp-vs-`gv` order are NOT refused: live reaches them); a signal is never owned; deps must be an array; subPos must be an array with one entry per dep (each an int >= 0, and per source a permutation of 0..n-1); ownerPos must be an int >= -1, exactly -1 when ownerId is null, and per owner a permutation of 0..n-1; a snapshot without subPos / ownerPos is refused; a null / non-object record throws a named TypeError. Snapshots carry live node ids, so a snapshot holding any node id past 0x3FFFFFFF (a node created after the registry's first 2^30 - 1, including in a registry restored at the cap that then grew) snapshots fine but restore() refuses it -- fail closed, by design (D-F); once those nodes are disposed, a NEW snapshot of that registry restores again (the old snapshot still holds the id and stays refused). Options must be a plain object with own keys fnsById / handles / config only -- an unknown key throws with a did-you-mean hint; bodies are looked up only as own properties of fnsById. Rejected structures: a signal with deps, an effect as a dep source, a signal as owner, a self owner, owner cycles, and a dep id missing from the snapshot on any record (dirty and never-read computeds included). opts.handles is filled only after the rebuild succeeds; a failed restore leaves it untouched. A snapshot taken after a registry's node-id counter wrapped (ids <= 0) is rejected (fail closed). A dep cycle among clean computeds is NOT refused: live can emit one (a computed whose body catches a CycleError from a partner), and the restored graph reproduces live exactly, including live's own CycleError ("CycleError: Circular dependency detected.") on the next read after a write to a dep (LEDGER #42, fixed in FIX-T; residual: a pool larger than the pre-walk stack limit still overflows the stack with a RangeError first).
// The snapshot records the registry clock (`gv`), the next node id (`nextId`) and every node's `evalVersion` / `markEpoch`, and restore copies them (the clock and next id exactly), so every freshness check in a restored graph answers as live's does (within the limits above): a restored effect no longer re-fires where live would not, and one that absorbed its own write is still due its re-run. The LIVE 2^31 dormancy band (the 32-bit version wrap) is unchanged and a restore reproduces it; the old restore-only wrap re-fire is gone.
// Box nodes carry FLAG_BOX (128): onGraphMutation op 1 / 2 flags are 160 (signalBox) / 129 (computedBox); callables stay 32 / 1 / 2.

interface Signal<T> {
  (): T;                             // tracked read
  peek(): T;                         // untracked read
  set(value: T): void;
  update(fn: (prev: T) => T): void;
  subscribe(fn: (value: T) => void): Dispose;
}

interface Computed<T> {
  (): T;                             // tracked read
  peek(): T;                         // untracked read
  subscribe(fn: (value: T) => void): Dispose;
}

interface SignalBox<T> {             // 1.5.0 -- non-callable, allocation-light
  get(): T;                          // tracked read
  set(value: T): void;
  peek(): T;                         // untracked read
  update(fn: (prev: T) => T): void;
  subscribe(fn: (value: T) => void): Dispose;
}

interface ComputedBox<T> {           // 1.5.0
  get(): T;                          // tracked read
  peek(): T;                         // untracked read
  subscribe(fn: (value: T) => void): Dispose;
}

type Dispose = () => void;

interface NodeDescriptor {           // yielded by forEachObserver / forEachSource / describe
  id: number;                        // stable per-allocation id (1.1.5); dedupe + re-walk key
  kind: "signal" | "computed" | "effect";
  value: unknown;                    // node's current value
}

interface RegistryConfig {
  maxNodes?: number;                 // default 1024 (ledger under "lazy")
  maxLinks?: number;                 // default maxNodes * 4 (ledger under "lazy")
  prealloc?: "eager" | "lazy";       // default "eager" (1.3.0): up-front vs on-demand pool construction
  maxFlushPasses?: number;           // default 100
  onCapacityExceeded?: "throw" | "grow";  // default "throw"; "grow" = chunked refill, ledger doubles, 16x link ceiling
}

interface RegistryStats {            // 13 keys as of 1.5.0
  signals: number;
  computeds: number;
  effects: number;
  activeLinks: number;
  pooledLinks: number;
  linkPoolCapacity: number;          // ledger; doubles under "grow"
  nodePoolCapacity: number;          // ledger; doubles under "grow"
  nodePoolPopulation: number;        // 1.5.0: TRUE constructed node count (nodePool.length); 0 under lazy prealloc
  linkPoolPopulation: number;        // 1.5.0: TRUE constructed link count (linkPool.length); 0 under lazy prealloc
  activeNodes: number;               // live gauge
  totalAllocations: number;          // 1.4.0: cumulative node acquires; zeroed by destroy(), kept by reset()
  totalDisposals: number;            // 1.4.0: cumulative node disposals; totalAllocations - totalDisposals === activeNodes
  poolGrowths: number;               // 1.4.0: cumulative pool-growth chunks; 0 if eager pool sized right
}

class CapacityError extends Error {
  kind: "nodes" | "links";
  capacity: number;
}
```

## Watchers (added in v1.1)

Three composable watcher primitives, all built from `effect` + `untrack`. Tree-shakeable.

### watch(source, callback, options?)

Fires callback on every change of the projected source value.

- **Signature**: `watch<T>(source: () => T, callback: (newValue: T, oldValue: T | undefined, stop: () => void) => void, options?: { immediate?: boolean }): () => void`
- **Returns**: dispose function. Idempotent. Safe to call synchronously inside the callback. The first call drops the last observed value, `source`, `callback` and the engine dispose handle, so a kept stop handle retains none of them; later calls are no-ops. Stopped wins: `stop()` called inside `source()` means the callback does not run after it and the value slots are not re-populated (through 1.5.2 the callback still fired after `stop()` with `(v, prev)`, with or without `immediate`, and the value was re-retained). A watcher disposed by its OWNER (a parent effect disposed first) keeps all four (value, `source`, `callback`, engine handle) until its stop handle is called (safe, releases everything) or dropped, as a raw `effect()` dispose handle keeps its registry.
- **Baseline commit order**: each fire reads the new value and the previous baseline into locals and commits the new value as the baseline BEFORE invoking the callback. A callback that throws therefore cannot leave a stale `oldValue`: with `s = signal(0)`, a callback that throws once on `s.set(1)` reports `(2, 1)` on the next `s.set(2)` (1.5.2 reported `(2, 0)`).
- **options.immediate**: when `true`, callback fires once on registration with `oldValue = undefined`. Default `false`.
- **Equality guard**: uses `Object.is(newValue, oldValue)` internally to avoid firing when the projected value is unchanged across dep mutations. Critical for raw getter sources like `() => health() <= 0` -- many dep changes can produce the same boolean. Wrapping the source in `computed()` would achieve the same via the computed's own equality check.
- **UNINITIALIZED sentinel**: uses `Symbol("watch.uninitialized")` instead of `undefined` to detect first-run. This means `signal(undefined)` is correctly distinguished from "watcher hasn't fired yet".
- **Callback reads are untracked**: the callback can read other signals without registering them as dependencies.
- **Stop in callback**: third callback argument is a stop handle. Safe to call at any point including synchronously during the immediate fire (the `wantsStopEarly` flag defers dispose until after the effect is registered).
- **Allocation profile**: 3 closures at registration (stop, effect body, hoisted untrack body). **Zero allocations per fire** -- the untrack body is hoisted with `currentNewValue` as shared mutable state. Hot-path safe at 120fps.

### when(predicate, callback)

Fires callback exactly once when predicate first returns truthy, then auto-disposes.

- **Signature**: `when(predicate: () => unknown, callback: () => void): () => void`
- **Returns**: dispose function. Useful for cancelling before predicate fires; idempotent; no-op after callback has fired. Once the watcher has fired or been cancelled, the handle drops the engine dispose handle (through 1.5.2 it kept it, so a kept handle retained the whole registry even when predicate and callback held nothing of it). The handle also releases `predicate` and `callback`, so a kept handle retains nothing of the watcher. Stopped wins: `cancel()` called inside the predicate on a later run means the callback does not run, even if that run returns truthy (through 1.5.2 it still fired). A callback that throws on a later fire (not at registration) skips the auto-dispose: the throw propagates out of the write, later writes do not refire, and the handle keeps the live effect (and predicate / callback) until `cancel()`, which releases everything (same on 1.5.2). A watcher disposed by its OWNER keeps the engine handle, predicate and callback until the handle is called (safe) or dropped.
- **Synchronous fire**: if predicate is already truthy at registration, callback fires synchronously and watcher disposes immediately (same `wantsStopEarly` pattern as `watch`).
- **One-shot guarantee**: internal `done` flag protects against double-fire; it is what stops a re-fire after a callback throws on a later fire (the effect stays live and later writes re-run it).
- **Callback reads are untracked.**
- **Truthy/falsy semantics**: standard JS truthy check. `0`, `""`, `null`, `undefined`, `false`, `NaN` do not trigger; everything else does.
- **Allocation profile**: 2 closures at registration (stop, effect body). **Zero allocations per check** -- `untrack(callback)` passes the user's callback directly without wrapping. Hot-path safe at 120fps.

### whenAsync(predicate)

Promise variant of `when`.

- **Signature**: `whenAsync(predicate: () => unknown): Promise<void>`
- **Returns**: Promise that resolves when predicate first becomes truthy.
- **Implementation**: `return new Promise((resolve) => when(predicate, resolve))`.
- **Foot-gun**: promise never rejects once registered. A predicate that throws on its first evaluation (at registration) rejects it with that error. One exception, as `effect()` documents: outside any batch or flush, if another body that evaluation ran (e.g. a computed it read) wrote a value the predicate had already read (its own writes are absorbed), the predicate re-runs at once and that re-run decides: a throw rejects with the re-run's error, a truthy result resolves, a falsy one drops the first error and the promise stays pending -- unless that same drain disposes the predicate's effect (before the re-run, which then does not run, or during or after a falsy one), which rejects with the first error. A later throw surfaces from the write (or the enclosing batch) that triggered it and the promise stays pending. If predicate never becomes truthy, promise never settles. Use `Promise.race` for timeout: `Promise.race([whenAsync(p), timeoutPromise])`.
- **! HOT-PATH WARNING**: `new Promise(...)` is a heap allocation. Each call allocates 1 Promise + 1 executor closure + Promise infrastructure (resolve fn, microtask state) + 2 closures from internal `when` call. This is unavoidable -- Promises require heap allocation by spec. **Do NOT call per frame.** Use for high-level orchestration (boot sequences, scene transitions, awaiting user input). For 60/120fps logic, use `when(predicate, callback)` directly -- it's zero-GC.

### Architecture note

None of these touch the reactive engine -- no `FLAG_WATCHER` on `ReactiveNode`, no extension to the object pool, no new internal primitive. They compose entirely from public API. This is the test that the core engine is structurally complete: when a higher-level pattern can be built without extending the engine, the engine has enough.

### Allocation profile summary

| Primitive | At registration | Per fire / check |
|---|---|---|
| `watch` | 3 closures | 0 |
| `when` | 2 closures | 0 |
| `whenAsync` | 1 Promise + executor + Promise internals + 2 closures (from `when`) | 0 |

The deliberate engineering for `watch`'s "0 per fire" is the hoisted `untrackedFire` closure with `currentNewValue` shared mutable state -- see source comment in `watch.js`. Inline arrow function inside the effect body would allocate per fire and break the zero-GC contract.

## Benchmark snapshot (1.6.0 dev, Signal.js a7202c9b, node v26.8.2, Apple M4 Pro, 10 reps)

Tier REPORTED: measurements, not a law; they gate nothing. Time only: no heap figure is published (see the withdrawal below). Zero-GC for lite-signal is gated by deterministic checks, not by these tables: `npm run test:torture` (lite-leak + lite-gc-profiler), the `node:test` GC-count rows, and the Tier 2b perf gate. Host: 2026-11-23 / 2026-11-24, quiet host on AC power, 10 reps per engine; medians in ms, lower is better. Engines: alien-signals 3.2.1, reflex-quant 1.2.0, @preact/signals-core 1.14.4, solid-js 1.9.15. Every table below is cut from `bench/results-1.6.0/` (provenance in its `README.md`).

Andrii js-reactivity-benchmark position (current; upstream's own protocol and hosts, not the local protocol in this section's heading). Upstream's own table of Andrii Volynets' js-reactivity-benchmark (sourceCommit f0d456c, rendered 2026-11-16, node v24.15.0 linux/x64, 24 machine shards, 3 machine rounds, 30 participants, 29 ranked; score = family-balanced geomean of time / per-test best over the 34 shared core scenarios) places lite-signal 1.5.2 8th of 29 at 1.91 (3-machine-set range 1.88-1.92). reflex-quant is 1st at 1.03, alien-signals 2nd at 1.20, reflex 3rd at 1.25, @reactively 1.63, Preact Signals 1.63, @vue/reactivity 3.6 RC 1.65, anod 1.83; rescript-signals is 9th at 1.92. reflex-quant has the lowest median on 27 of 51 tests (21 of 34 core; this repo's count over upstream's samples) and 16 decisive wins (upstream's paired-range rule); lite-signal has 0 lowest-median tests and 0 decisive wins. The earlier "4th of 15" was the 1.5.0-beta result on Andrii's host (47 tests, plain geomean of ms); the field is now 30 participants with different scoring and hosts. 1.6.0 PROJECTED, cross-host: 1.907 / 1.903 -> 8th, inside 1.5.2's own range 1.88-1.92: no measurable change. The alien-normalised M1 (D-b169-1 Q4a) gives 1.825 / 1.650 (7th / 6th) but misses the known 1.5.2 point by -4.3% / -13.3%; no rank claim rests on it. Local legs (Andrii's harness, clone 12f169b, 7 adapters, Apple M4 Pro, node v26.8.2 / v24.15.0, 2026-11-24, run count 1 per leg; geomean time / alien-signals over 51 rows): 1.6.0 / 1.5.2 lazy 0.983 / 0.979 (flat); eager-1.6 / eager 1.5.2 1.034 / 1.076 (1.6.0 eager is SLOWER); alien-signals lowest median on 44 / 42 of 51 rows. The reset adapter (reset() keeps the warmed pool where upstream destroys and rebuilds; lazy 0.832 / 0.889, eager 0.890 / 0.823 vs the 1.6.0 destroy adapters) is an adapter choice and is never ranked against upstream's table. Tier REPORTED. Provenance and formulas: `bench/andrii/2026-11-24/README.md`.

Band rule: spread = (max - min) / median of the 10 per-rep medians; the pair band is the larger of the two engines' spreads; delta = (other - lite) / other, so + means lite faster. A |delta| at or under the band is "inside the band", never a win or a loss. A win count counts only leads outside the band.

Microscope (`bench/benchmark.mjs`, six first-party shapes; isolated-per-engine, round-robin, one cold process per engine per rep, 5 engines, HEAD 9ccc286), median ms (`bench/results-1.6.0/microscope-time.txt`):

| BROADCAST     | 285.49  | 395.59  | 544.35  | 1068.22 | 366.07       |
| DEEP CHAIN    | 172.69  | 87.94   | 149.13  | 550.03  | 82.58        |

Lowest median per scenario: reflex-quant on 4 of 6 (KAIROS, DEEP CHAIN, DYNAMIC DAG, SELECTIVE DAG), lite on 2 of 6 (BROADCAST, MUX); none of reflex-quant's 4 leads over the runner-up engine is outside the band, one of lite's 2 is. lite vs preact: lite ahead outside the band on 4/6, preact ahead on 2 (DEEP CHAIN, DYNAMIC DAG). lite vs solid: lite ahead outside the band on 6/6.

Losses outside the band, stated plainly: DEEP CHAIN against alien, reflex-quant and preact (256-deep chain; alien and reflex-quant about 2x faster than lite in this run), KAIROS, DYNAMIC DAG and SELECTIVE DAG against reflex-quant, DYNAMIC DAG against preact, and the creation, deep and layered rows of the 47-row tables below (e.g. sweep `createDataSignals` -560.4% with a band of 18.7%, `deepPropagation` -84.9% with a band of 6.3%, both alien ahead). Recursive JS-stack computed resolution is the known weak spot.

47-row mirror (`bench/results-1.6.0/mirror-bands.txt`, `mirror-report.txt`; isolated-per-engine shared harness: one cold process per engine ran all 47 rows in a fixed order, capture 20261123T221116Z-c3010561, HEAD 9ccc286). lite vs alien: lite ahead outside the band on 3/47 rows (`manySourcesIntoOneComputedEffectWithDirect` +12.0%, `manySourcesIntoOneComputedEffect` +12.4%, `updateComputations1000to1` +17.0%), inside the band on 6, alien ahead on 38. lite vs reflex-quant: lite ahead outside the band on 3/47, inside on 5, reflex-quant ahead on 39. Lowest median per row: alien-signals 33 rows, reflex-quant 10, lite 3, 1 tie.

47-row sweep (`bench/results-1.6.0/sweep-bands.txt`, `sweep-report.txt`; isolated-per-row, every engine and row in its own cold process, capture 20261124T001531Z-02a0b456, HEAD 0fffc59). lite vs alien: lite ahead outside the band on 3/47 rows (the same three: +18.8%, +16.3%, +11.4%), inside the band on 7, alien ahead on 37. lite vs reflex-quant: lite ahead outside the band on 0/47, inside on 5, reflex-quant ahead on 42. Lowest median per row: alien-signals 28 rows, reflex-quant 16, lite 1 (`updateComputations1000to1`, a lead inside the band), 2 ties. The sweep log flags 18 lite / alien rows over an 8% spread; those are bands, not point deltas.

Named rows: `1000x12 - 4 sources - dynamic (large web app)` has alien ahead outside the band in both protocols (mirror -45.4%, band 2.3%; sweep -44.4%, band 2.2%). `1000x5 - 25 sources (wide dense)` is inside the band against alien in both (mirror -1.2%, band 3.1%; sweep -3.0%, band 3.4%) and reflex-quant is ahead of lite on it in both (mirror -7.0%, band 2.8%; sweep -25.9%, band 13.9%).

The two 47-row protocols disagree beyond their noise bands on 24 of 47 rows (lite vs alien delta differing by more than the larger pair band). Example: `updateComputations1to2` is +2.2% (band 5.7%, inside the band) in the mirror and -30.0% (band 7.5%, alien ahead outside the band) in the sweep. Cite a protocol with every figure.

Heap column withdrawn: the earlier column read heapUsed after a forced GC before each run and again at the run's end with no closing GC, so past one young generation it showed young-generation fill, not the run's allocation. This release publishes benchmark time only.

Retracking verified correct by `retracking.difftest.mjs` (20,000 direct + 10,000 batched writes, 0 disagreements vs published 1.1.5).
`prealloc: "lazy"` trades a little first-construction allocation on the dynamic shapes
for a smaller resident heap and faster cold start; steady state identical.

## Common idioms

```js
// Glitch-free diamond
const a = signal(1);
const b = computed(() => a() + 1);
const c = computed(() => a() * 2);
const d = computed(() => b() + c());   // re-evaluates exactly once per a.set

// Conditional subscription (b only tracked when flag is true)
const flag = signal(true);
const a = signal(1);
const b = signal(2);
const sum = computed(() => flag() ? a() + b() : a());

// Scheduler integration (rAF batching)
let queued = false;
effect(() => render(state()), {
  scheduler: run => {
    if (queued) return;
    queued = true;
    requestAnimationFrame(() => { queued = false; run(); });
  }
});

// Sandboxed plugin
const sandbox = createRegistry({ maxNodes: 256, onCapacityExceeded: "throw" });
plugin(sandbox.signal, sandbox.computed, sandbox.effect);
// later:
sandbox.destroy();   // entire reactive world invalidated (no cleanups; sandbox.reset() runs them)

// 1.2.1: push-based devtools via onGraphMutation
// Single listener; opcodes 1=create, 2=dispose, 3=link-add, 4=link-remove, 5=recompute.
// Allocation-free dispatch with just three integers.
const unsubscribe = onGraphMutation((opcode, intA, intB) => {
  switch (opcode) {
    case 1: devtools.onNodeCreate(intA, intB);   break;   // intA=id, intB=flags
    case 2: devtools.onNodeDispose(intA);        break;
    case 3: devtools.onLinkAdd(intA, intB);      break;   // intA=source.id, intB=target.id
    case 4: devtools.onLinkRemove(intA, intB);   break;
    case 5: devtools.onRecompute(intA);          break;
  }
});
// Stop listening -- any order; the newest still-live listener stays active (none left: zero-cost state).
unsubscribe();

// 1.2.1: walk the owner tree (cascade-disposal domains)
//   forEachOwned + ownerOf complement forEachObserver + forEachSource:
//   the dep/sub edges show DATA FLOW; the owner edges show LIFETIME BINDING.
function dumpOwnerTree(handle, depth = 0) {
  const d = describe(handle);
  if (!d) return;
  console.log(" ".repeat(depth * 2), d.kind, d.id);
  forEachOwned(d, (child) => dumpOwnerTree(child, depth + 1));
}
```

## File layout

- `Signal.js`              -- full implementation, single file.
- `Signal.d.ts`          -- TypeScript declarations for all public API.
- `test/01-core.test.mjs`     -- signal/computed/effect basics, equality, untrack.
- `test/02-topology.test.mjs` -- diamonds, chains, fan-out/in, cycle detection.
- `test/03-pool.test.mjs`     -- capacity errors, grow policy, pool reuse.
- `test/04-zero-gc.test.mjs`  -- heap retention (run with --expose-gc).
- `test/05-scheduler.test.mjs` -- scheduler races, dispose, gen counter, version wrap.
- `test/06-nested-objects.test.mjs` -- nested-object & reference-identity behaviours.
- `test/07-dispose.test.mjs` -- universal disposal: registry.dispose(api).
- `test/08-watch.test.mjs` -- new watch reactivity tests.
- `test/09-conformance.test.mjs` -- johnsoncodehk/reactive-framework-test-suite conformance fixes tests.
- `test/10-is-tracking.test.mjs` -- `isTracking()` across observer bodies, untracked windows, and outside any observer.
- `test/11-adopted-reactive.test.mjs` -- engine-agnostic edge cases adopted from the wider ecosystem (alien-signals link-integrity #226-228, equality-predicate corners, `update()`/`peek()`/`subscribe` contracts).
- `test/12-coverage.test.mjs` -- targeted public-surface + hot-path branch coverage (top-level routing, clean-read short-circuit, tail severance, scheduler ABA); owner-tree block capability-gated.
- `test/13-introspection.test.mjs` -- observer-lifecycle surface: `hasObservers`, `observeObservers` auto-pause, `forEach*` enumeration (10 tests).
- `test/14-lifecycle-teardown.test.mjs` -- effect-teardown guards: stopped effect doesn't re-subscribe to a signal read later in the same run, self-dispose leaves no orphan link, throwing setup leaves no live subscription (4 tests).
- `test/15-owner-lazy-alloc.test.mjs` -- owner-adoption contract for the 1.2.0 owner tree (lazy signals never adopted; observers still auto-disposed); capability-gated, skipped on 1.1.x (4 tests).
- `test/16-alien-parity.test.mjs` -- differential guards vs alien-signals@3.2.0 fixed-bug classes: cleanup reads create no deps, inner write doesn't block computed-chain propagation, dynamic dep-set correct under dirty-check (3 tests).
- `test/17-reactivity.test.mjs` -- behavioral suite over universal signal-system bug classes (subscription lifecycle, cleanup ordering, stale-dep tracking, batching, equality, nested invalidation, memory, sync async-boundary, scheduler/loops, + differential-review additions); SSR is N/A (~30 tests).
- `test/18-identity.test.mjs` -- node identity (1.1.5): `nodeId`/`describe`, descriptor `id`, re-walkable descriptors, non-perturbing (5 tests).
- `test/19-v12-additions.test.mjs` -- 1.2.0 surface coverage: shared-peek, owner-adoption rule, pre-batch revert (24 tests).
- `test/20-axis-stress.test.mjs` -- eight orthogonal stress axes (batch-under-exception, connect/disconnect re-entrancy, untrack vs owner cascade, etc.) (23 tests).
- `test/21-perf-pins.test.mjs` -- 1.2.1 construction-shape + ABA-guard pins (6 tests).
- `test/22-mutation-hook.test.mjs` -- 1.2.1 `onGraphMutation` registration + opcode emission (12 tests).
- `test/23-owner-introspection.test.mjs` -- `ownerOf`, `forEachOwned`, gen-guarded introspection (14 tests).
- `test/24-signalbox.test.mjs` -- staged for 1.5.0; all tests `{skip: true}` on 1.2.x.
- `test/25-devtools-real-boot.test.mjs` -- 1.2.2: real `Devtools.js` boot against the engine, ghost-contract pin, `stats()` shape pin (10 tests).
- `test/26-free-list-invariant.test.mjs` -- 1.2.2: the audit's clean-free-list invariant, asserted by inspecting freshly-allocated nodes (4 tests).
- `bench/benchmark.mjs`       -- anti-DCE throughput harness (ops/s; prints to stdout; `bench/results.txt` is a checked-in captured table from 2016 Intel / Node 22 / pre-v3, kept as history, and the script does not write it; the current time-only results are in `bench/results-1.6.0/`).
- `bench/results-1.6.0/` -- time-only results on the final engine (REPORTED tier, 10 reps, Signal.js a7202c9b): `README.md` (provenance), `microscope-time.txt`, `mirror-report.txt` + `mirror-bands.txt`, `sweep.txt` + `sweep-report.txt` + `sweep-bands.txt`, `cross-protocol.txt`, `bands.log`.
- `bench/benchmarkReactive.mjs` -- cross-framework reactivity suite vs alien-signals, preact, vue-reactivity, solid (resultsReactive.txt).
- `bench/dispose-recycle.mjs` -- 1.2.2 targeted microbench: create/dispose/recreate cycle (the free-list invariant audit target).
- `bench/torture/` -- the complete **25-scenario superset (24 semantic + 1 opt-in soak)** behind one runner (`run.mjs`), two groups, forward-compatible through 1.10. Every scenario feature-detects and SKIPS cleanly below the engine version that introduces its feature, so the whole set is safe on the 1.5.0 engine and stays green from 1.4.x forward. `semantic` (deterministic, fast, asserts on MEANING; CI on every commit) -- the **18 that execute on the 1.5.x engine** (the nine first listed here, then `owner-torture`, `retrack-dispose-torture`, `error-torture`, `contract-torture`, `interop-torture`, `deep-chain-torture`, `zerogc-torture`, `introspect-torture`, `lifecycle-torture`): `oracle-fuzzer` (every computed vs an independent uncached reference, 400 seeds x 120 ops), `glitch-hunter` (glitch freedom + exact wakeups), `work-accounting` (minimum body-execution counts over 10 topologies), `concurrent-storm` (8 reentrancy / flush-ordering contracts), `scheduler-storm` (gen-bound thunk ABA guard, FLAG_QUEUED coalescing, throwing-scheduler containment), `box-torture` (1.5.0: signalBox/computedBox interop -- the oracle differential fuzz with every node realised as callable OR box, plus box-only subscribe/update and the allocation-light representation contract), `async-torture` (watch / when / whenAsync contracts + a 300-seed projection-guard storm), `capacity-torture` (the fail-closed pool boundary -- exact ceilings, re-throw-on-read, `grow` crossing the same boundary), `op-accounting` (structural work counted from the engine's own `onGraphMutation` opcode lane, not wall-clock); plus `snapshot-torture` (1.6.0 `snapshot()` / `restore()`: clean-bit round-trip fuzz with an op-log clean oracle and coverage floors, fail-closed battery, D-A..D-D rulings; executes on 1.6.0, skips below); plus `reset-torture` (1.6.0 `reset()`: 0 B and 0 GCs per reset, must-fail control, lite-leak stale-handle witness); plus `scope-torture` (1.6.0 `createScope`; executes on 1.6.0, skips below); plus **3 that skip cleanly** as later-version features: `flush-torture` (1.8.0 `flushStrategy`), `cleanup-return-torture` (1.9.0 effect-return cleanup), `dispose-torture` (1.10.0 `Symbol.dispose`). `soak` (opt-in, ~30 s, asserts on VALUES: the 2^31 dormancy band at full distance): only `wraparound-torture` (`TORTURE_WRAPAROUND=1`, exit 78 = skip) remains; `graph-fuzzer` and `torture-soak` were retired 2026-10-20 (absorbed by the bench/soak GRAPH lane) and `scheduler-bench` on 2026-10-29 (absorbed by the bench/soak SCHEDULER lane, whose queue is synchronous, so real microtask timing is witnessed only by test/05-scheduler.test.mjs). Runner spawns each scenario as a child process (several assert on global pool accounting) and passes `--expose-gc` unconditionally. Verdict rules (AUD-H2, `test/111`): a scenario passes only with exit 0 AND a `  PASS: ` line on stdout; exit 77 is a skip only below the scenario's version floor and FAILS at or above it, the floor key being the higher of the `package.json` version and the surface `Signal.d.ts` declares (`bench/torture/helpers/surface.mjs`); an unreadable input exits 2. `harness/conformance.mjs` (`test/112`) exits 2 on fewer than 178 executed conformance or 18 behavioral cases, or a KNOWN_FAIL case absent / skipped in a run; in single-engine mode a KNOWN_FAIL case that passes exits 1. Scripts: `npm run torture`, `torture:semantic`, `torture:soak`.
- `bench/torture/helpers/index.mjs` -- shared torture infrastructure: seeded `mulberry32` (failures replay from their seed), `soakRegistry` / `fixedRegistry`, `createReport` (collects failures rather than throwing on the first), and `VALUE_POOL`, the adversarial value domain carrying the pairs where candidate equality definitions disagree (`Object.is` vs `===` on NaN and -0/0; `===` vs `==` on 0/""/false/"0" and null/undefined). Dependency-free and side-effect-free by contract: importing it must not touch the default registry.
- `bench/run-all-bench.sh` + `bench/aggregate.mjs` -- cold-process-per-engine protocol + per-scenario aggregation.
- `harness/run.mjs`          -- dispatcher for the run-on-demand probes (field, dispose, churn, owner, creation, mint, all).
- `harness/mint-anatomy.mjs` -- mint+dispose cycle allocation anatomy (`mint` / `mint --verify`): per-op all-space vs new-space heap bytes for every creation primitive on a pre-grown throw-policy registry, fresh child per (variant, warmup) cell. Documents the 264 B/op callable cycle vs 56 B/op signalBox and the ALL-space accounting rule (a new-space-only witness undercounts by ~56 B/op of pre-TurboFan closure-feedback -- the LS-06 correction). `--verify` applies relative pins P1..P5.
- `harness/fieldkit.mjs`     -- single-file portable verify + cold-child A/B bench across six shapes.
- `harness/owner-hazard-repro.mjs` -- async-gap owner-recycling hazard verdict (cited by getOwner/runWithOwner).
- `harness/VersionMatrix/`   -- cold-process-per-version performance regression gate (run by hand: `npm run gate`; no publish hook).
- `harness/ProfilerTools/`   -- profiler-signal x devtools composition harness (wired as test:harness).
- `harness/attic/`           -- parked one-off probes (the 1.2.0->1.2.1 shape-regression hunt); wired into nothing.
- `demo/index.html`           -- interactive visualization of the reactive graph.
